subject: Harmonizing hosted API latency SLO measurement windows (p50/p95)
messages:
From: Eli Mercer <eli@brightlane.io>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: sales_ops@brightlane.io
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify p50/p95 measurement window for hosted API (audit ask)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the performance looked promising. Our compliance and SRE teams are preparing Brightlane's security and SLA assessment ahead of procurement, and they've asked for a clear statement of how Redwood measures latency SLOs (specifically p50 and p95) for the hosted API. They want to know: 

- The exact measurement window (rolling 5m/1h/day?) used for both p50 and p95.
- What samples are included/excluded (warmup, retries, synthetic probes, burst carveouts).
- Regional alignment: we operate in us-east and us-west; audit wants to ensure the metric aggregation is region-aware.

I've attached the draft SLO language our procurement team will include in the contract — can your team confirm what evidence we can provide for a SOC-like audit (e.g., sampling dashboards, canary snapshots, raw percentile export)?

Can we aim to sync this week? Our preferred timeline is to finalize language so our legal team can review by 2026-05-25.

Best,
Eli Mercer
Head of Platform Reliability
Brightlane Systems

Attachments: Brightlane_SLO_Draft_20260518.pdf

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Eli Mercer <eli@brightlane.io>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 measurement window for hosted API (audit ask)

Eli — thanks for the clear ask and the draft. Looping in Lauren (Customer Success) and Kimberly (Product/Policy) so we can give you a consolidated response and an evidence plan.

High level answers up front (we'll follow with details & attachments):
- Measurement windows: Redwood reports p50/p95 on a rolling 1h window for operational dashboards, and we compute contractual monthly aggregates for SLA purposes. For transient burst carveouts we use a separate burst-detection pipeline (see attachment).
- Sampling: production requests are included; synthetic probes and system-level probes are excluded from contractual calculations. Retries are deduped at the API gateway level before percentile computation.
- Regional aggregation: p50/p95 are computed per-region by default; contractual commitments are scoped to the region of the customer (we can provide per-region exports for us-east/us-west).

Immediate next steps:
1) Kimberly will list the evidence artifacts we can hand over (dashboards, CSV exports, canary snapshots).
2) Lauren will propose wording tweaks to your draft SLO so it maps to our measurement artifacts.
3) I'll prepare a short mutual action plan and a signed evidence checklist for your legal team.

Can we schedule a 30-min call Thu 14 May 10:00–10:30 PT? If that doesn't work, Friday morning also looks clear.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

Attachment: slo-evidence-checklist.csv

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, Eli Mercer <eli@brightlane.io>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 measurement window for hosted API (audit ask)

Eli, Vanessa — quick notes from CS side after skimming the draft:

- Suggest explicit language for two measurement horizons in the contract: 
  * "Contractual monthly percentile": derived from hourly rolling aggregates, computed on calendar-month boundaries for billing/SLR.
  * "Operational percentile": rolling 1h for alerting/ops (not used to compute credits).

- For carveouts: include a short clause that transient network events (e.g., provider peering loss > 2x baseline) may be excluded with evidence and joint review. Define an "evidence package" (timestamped canary snapshots, request-id traces, aggregated histograms).

- Evidence handover: We can provide a zipped export of raw request latencies (time series and request-level samples) for the requested period, plus canary snapshots at hourly resolution for the 72 hours around any flagged incident. We will redact customer payloads.

Action items I can own if Brightlane approves:
- Draft contract wording for the two-horizon approach.
- Prepare a sample evidence zip and a one-page handoff document for legal review.

If acceptable, I'll send the proposed redlines and the sample evidence package by Monday 18 May.

— Lauren
Director, Customer Success
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Eli Mercer <eli@brightlane.io>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harmonizing hosted API latency SLO measurement windows (p50/p95) — mutual action plan

Eli — thanks for the sync today. Per our call, attaching the mutual action plan and the evidence checklist for your procurement/legal team. Summary below (short version for your counsel):

1) Measurement definitions (what Redwood will commit to):
- Operational: rolling 1h window for p50/p95 used for monitoring and alerts.
- Contractual: monthly contractual SLO computed from hourly aggregates; credits (if any) are applied to the monthly contract window.

2) Sampling & exclusions:
- Included: production user requests to the hosted API (authenticated application traffic).
- Excluded: synthetic probes, internal backend-to-backend health checks, and deduplicated retry attempts recorded by the gateway.
- Transient carveouts: Brightlane may request a joint review for events affecting >5% of region capacity during a contiguous 30-minute span; evidence package required.

3) Regional alignment:
- We compute percentiles per-region by default. For contract language, we will scope the SLA to the customer's primary region (Brightlane: us-east). We will provide per-region exports on request.

4) Evidence we will provide (attached checklist):
- Hourly canary snapshots (72-hour window around flagged events)
- Raw request-latency CSV for the relevant time range (redacted)
- Dashboard links and percentile rollups (read-only)
- Request-id trace samples for up to 5 sampled requests per incident

5) Timeline:
- Redwood to deliver contract redlines and sample evidence package by Mon 2026-05-24 (Lauren).
- Brightlane legal to review and revert by Tue 2026-05-25.

Attachments included: m-a-p-20260520.xlsx (mutual action plan), slo-evidence-checklist.csv, Brightlane_SLO_Draft_20260518.pdf

If that matches your expectations I'll upload the evidence bundle to the secure link (Ops ticket OPS-212) and share access for your legal team.

Next immediate ask: could you confirm that Brightlane will accept the two-horizon wording (operational vs contractual) so we can bake it into the contract? A simple yes/no by EOD Friday would keep our timeline intact.

Thanks — Vanessa
